{{Trail|Magic}}
This page documents the '''blessings''' that you can receive, typically by activating altars in temples. These are short-term blessings which act separately from long-term [[Skyrim:Standing Stone|Standing Stone]] effects, and do not overwrite or interact with them. Typically, you will want any blessings you come across, unless you are specifically trying to bolster one effect.

==Shrine Blessings==
Blessings are bestowed by praying at (activating) a shrine to the specified deity.
* Locations of the shrines of the Eight (or Nine) Divines, including those for [[Lore:Auriel|Auriel]] added by [[Skyrim:Dawnguard|Dawnguard]], are listed at [[Skyrim:Shrines|Shrines]].
* The Shrine of Nocturnal is located inside the [[Skyrim:The Ragged Flagon - Cistern|Ragged Flagon Cistern]], once you are midway through the [[Skyrim:Thieves Guild (faction)|Thieves Guild]] quest line.
You can only have one shrine blessing at a time. If you choose to pray at a second shrine, it will overwrite the previous blessing. Shrine blessings are active for a period of time measured in ''real'' time, not in-game time. So a blessing lasting 12 hours will be active during 12 playing hours.

{{Note|BloodoftheAncients|^3|{{Bug|The in-game description of the 'Blood of the Ancients' spell is not directly linked to its duration. The duration of the spell is calculated based on scripts and affixed to a specific day, while the description shows the effectively meaningless magnitude of the spell. This means that the Necromage perk, which increases the magnitude and duration of spells cast on undead (such as your vampiric self), causes the description in your 'spells - active effects' menu to display that its duration is increased by 25% (which in turn is caused by the perk's effect on magnitude, not duration), but the spell actually lasts only as long as calculated by the Chalice's Level.|nobullet=1}}}}

==Notes==
* Even if you betrayed Azura during [[Skyrim:The Black Star|The Black Star]], you will still be able to gain her blessing.
* Unlike other sources of Fortify Health, the Blessing of Arkay will not default the player to a minimum 1HP when the effect ends, so if you're under 25HP when the effect ends (either by passing enough time or replacing it with another blessing), you die.
* Blessings are considered to be "potion" effects with [[Skyrim:Survival Mode|Survival Mode]]{{CC}} enabled, and are thus modified by your level of [[Skyrim:Fatigue|Fatigue]].

{{Bug|With [[Skyrim:Dawnguard|Dawnguard]] installed, Voice of the Sky will prevent vampires (and their animal companions) from turning hostile. [[Skyrim:Vampire's Thrall|Thralls]] and [[Skyrim:Gargoyle|Gargoyles]] remain adversarial, however.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG|UDGP|2.0.5|trackerid=13482|The vampires had to be removed from the Prey Faction because it caused Voice of the Sky to make them docile when it wasn't supposed to.}}
{{Bug|For the player, all shrine blessings and the Blessing of the Stag Prince are scaled by any active [[Skyrim:Fortify Restoration|Fortify Restoration]] alchemy effect at the moment the blessing is applied. Scaled magnitudes stick until the blessing is removed or refreshed. In the 'Active Effects' list, the description will show the increased effect magnitude.|USKP|2.1.3|confirmed=1|modnotes=This is caused by the fact that the associated magic effects have their 'Magic Skill' field set to 'Restoration', which allows perk AlchemySkillBoosts to scale the spell magnitudes by (1 + RestorationPowerMod/100).|trackerid=18867}}
